business.title: Development and validation of an irradiation-free assay for routine diagnostic evaluation of individual radiosensitivity in personalized treatment
business.description: Approximately 50% of cancer patients receive radiotherapy (RT), yet clinicians lack reliable tools to predict treatment-related toxicity prior to therapy. Consequently, 5 to 10% of breast cancer patients develop late radiation-induced fibrosis, highlighting interindividual variability radiosensitivity. The Radiation-Induced Lymphocyte Apoptosis (RILA) test has been clinically validated as a predictive biomarker of intrinsic radiosensitivity to support adaptation of treatment according to individual radiosensitivity. Although the test only relies on peripheral blood sampling and a short analytical turnaround from venipuncture to results, its reliance on irradiation facilities has remained a major barrier to deployment. Here, we report the development and analytical validation of an irradiation-free and automated RILA workflow designed for routine use. Using blood samples from healthy donors and cancer patients, we demonstrate analytical equivalence between bleomycin- and irradiation-based RILA assays, robust RILA scores after pre-analytical delays of up to 72 h, and excellent agreement between automated and expert manual cytometry analysis. Transfer of the complete workflow to an independent biomedical laboratory further confirmed inter-laboratory reproducibility and clinical concordance. By removing technical barriers while preserving the clinical interpretability of RILA scores, this optimized workflow enables broad implementation of individual radiosensitivity testing and supports the integration of personalized treatment into clinical practice.

business.title: Arduino-controlled pulse electrodeposition for low-cost zinc coating on stainless steel
business.description: Advanced metallic coatings represent a primary frontier within surface science and industrial surface engineering. In this study, a highly cost-effective, additive-free pulse electrodeposition (PED) strategy is demonstrated for coating AISI 304 stainless-steel substrates with zinc, utilizing a simplified setup controlled via an Arduino microcontroller. The isolated effect of pulse frequency on the resulting coating architecture was systematically investigated across a range from 150 to 250 Hz while maintaining a strictly fixed peak current density, duty cycle, and deposition time. Stylus profilometry verified that all samples maintained a macromanaged, constant nominal thickness of approximately 8 µm, a stabilization trend fundamentally governed by Faraday’s Law of Electrolysis. However, comprehensive multi-instrument profiling via FESEM, XRF, EDS, XRD, and XPS revealed a profound, frequency-induced microstructural and chemical transition. At a lower frequency of 150 Hz, the deposit formed a dense, well-leveled, and continuous layer composed of uniform hexagonal zinc prisms. Conversely, escalating the PED frequency to 250 Hz triggered a distinctive "condensation effect," forcing the zinc to abandon planar growth and aggregate into isolated, high-relief island clusters separated by prominent bare substrate gaps. Bulk XRD structural refinement confirmed a highly phase-pure, primitive hexagonal close-packed crystal lattice ($$P{6}_{3}/mmc$$), while revealing a significant textural reorientation across the (101), (102), and (103) crystallographic planes alongside a reduction in crystallite size at elevated frequencies. Macroscopic XRF and localized EDS profiling cross-validated this morphological shift, capturing a pronounced escalation in the underlying substrate iron (Fe) signal at 250 Hz caused by electrical current lines constricting preferentially along high-energy substrate defects and metal kinks. Surface-sensitive XPS and Zn LMM Auger deconvolution successfully resolved three distinct surface-confined chemical states: metallic zinc ($$Zn$$), zinc oxide ($$ZnO$$), and zinc hydroxide ($$Zn{\left(OH\right)}_{2}$$). Quantitative analysis revealed a systematic, linear accumulation of $$Zn{\left(OH\right)}_{2}$$ at higher frequencies. This phase shift is driven by a cyclic interfacial alkalinization mechanism, wherein ultra-short pulse-off windows trap electrochemically generated hydroxyl ions ($${OH}^{-}$$) at the cathode interface, forcing the precipitation of a passive hydroxide interlayer that blocks normal epitaxial rain propagation. Ultimately, this research provides a definitive physical mechanism for frequency-tuned electrocrystallization, demonstrating that this low-cost, additive-free configuration can dynamically switch between fabricating continuous traditional metallurgical barrier films and tailoring high-surface-area micro-nanostructured cluster frameworks for advanced functional applications such as chemical sensors, photoelectrochemical solar cells, and energy storage systems.

science.title: Adjunctive vitamin D3 therapy enhances clinical response to tadalafil in men with erectile dysfunction: a randomized, placebo-controlled study
science.description: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is increasingly recognized as a sentinel marker of systemic vascular disease, characterized by impaired nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability and endothelial dysfunction. Emerging evidence suggests that vitamin D deficiency—a global health pandemic—compounds this pathology by exacerbating oxidative stress and downregulating endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS). While observational data link low vitamin D to ED, interventional evidence regarding its role as a therapeutic adjunct remains limited. To determine whether pharmacological correction of vitamin D deficiency synergistically enhances the efficacy of daily tadalafil in men with symptomatic ED. This triple-blind randomized clinical trial was conducted at two urology clinics in Mashhad, Iran. Forty men with ED (IIEF score < 25) and laboratory-confirmed vitamin D deficiency (10–30 ng/mL) were randomized (1:1) to receive either 5 mg daily tadalafil plus 50,000 IU of weekly vitamin D3 (Group A), or tadalafil plus a matched placebo (Group B) for 10 weeks. The primary outcome was the change in the IIEF scores. Multiple linear regression was employed to adjust for confounding factors. Baseline demographic characteristics and IIEF scores were comparable between the study arms. Following the 10-week intervention, Group A demonstrated significant superior improvements in the erectile function subdomain of IIEF score (21.7 ± 3.9 vs. 18.4 ± 2.4; p = 0.005) and total IIEF scores (52.8 ± 8.8 vs. 48.3 ± 4.5; p = 0.030) compared to Group B. Furthermore, 25% of the intervention group achieved complete resolution of ED symptoms, a threshold not reached by any member of the control group. After adjusting for baseline variables, vitamin D supplementation remained a significant independent predictor of clinical improvement (p = 0.001). Weekly high-dose vitamin D3 supplementation significantly potentiates the therapeutic efficacy of daily tadalafil. These findings advocate for the routine integration of vitamin D screening and correction into the diagnostic workup and management of organic ED to optimize both sexual and vascular health outcomes.

science.title: Nocturnal to diurnal switches of tuco-tucos (Ctenomys coludo) in semi-natural burrow systems inside the laboratory
science.description: Although many species are classified as strictly diurnal or nocturnal, the temporal distribution of daily activity can be flexible for several species. The subterranean rodent tuco-tuco (Ctenomys coludo) presents this flexibility, switching from diurnality to nocturnality when transferred from field to laboratory. Semi-natural environments (between field and lab) provide insights due to the partial maintenance of elements of both environments. In a sequence of previous studies, we have gradually explored distinct semi-natural conditions and our main goal here was to test if the nocturnal-to-diurnal switch could be reproduced in a controlled, minimalistic “mini-field” constructed inside the lab. These were glass boxes (50 × 50 × 90 cm) half-filled with soil where subterranean tuco-tucos could dig and establish galleries, as they do in nature, while environmental variables, such as temperature and food availability were controlled. Animals wore accelerometers and light-loggers to record activity and light exposure patterns, while video recordings monitored behaviors on the surface. 11 of 16 tuco-tucos switched abruptly to diurnal patterns upon transfer from cages to terrariums, with the phase of activity onsets and offsets switching to offset and onsets, respectively. Accelerometry data were subjected to behavioral classification analysis using a machine learning model prediction (HMM Hidden Markov Models) previously trained with tuco-tucos in standard cages. Because terrariums allowed subterranean tuco-tucos to express field behaviors refrained in cages, our video analysis provided additional validation to the HMM model. This analysis confirmed that the most rhythmic and the defining element of diurnal or nocturnal pattern in tuco-tucos are the high intensity activities and showed that these are behaviors such as digging and soil removal performed on the surface.
